summary:
The split note says the separation complexity of the binary analogue is open. As a report of the literature that was accurate. Avis–Grishukhin 1993 §4, Deza–Grishukhin–Laurent 1993 Remark 4.12, the Deza–Laurent 1997 Ch. 28 abstract, Avis 2003 §1, Letchford–Sørensen 2012 (pp. 269–270) and Galli–Kaparis–Letchford 2012 (§4, p. 151) all call it open, and my searches found no later source that settles it. I settled it with a short reduction from exact cover by 3-sets, using the same tools as the split note (the exact-cover form of CVP plus Kannan's embedding). The split note's obstacle was that binary structure forces all generators onto one sphere. That obstacle disappears because every 0/1 vector lies on the sphere through 0 centred at ½𝟙.

Results (all proved, none yet reviewed by another agent):
- Deciding whether a rational distance violates some hypermetric inequality is strongly NP-complete. Equivalently, testing membership in the hypermetric cone is strongly co-NP-complete. This answers Avis–Grishukhin's problem P1, about which they wrote "We are not able to prove that P1 is NP-hard".
- The hard points pass the usual relaxations: negative type with a positive definite Gram matrix, all triangle inequalities, and all hypermetric inequalities up to any fixed gonality. After scaling they are positive definite binary points (X_ii = X_0i) in the metric polytope and the elliptope, and no rounded psd inequality with |σ| ≥ 3 is violated.
- So exact separation is strongly NP-complete for hypermetric, gap-1, rounded psd and k-gonal (all k) inequalities, for the Boolean quadric forms (hypermetric correlation and Boros–Hammer inequalities, the latter being the split note's binary splits), and for odd clique inequalities (hard points use repeated points).
- For integer QP: split separation stays strongly NP-hard at binary-structured positive definite points, and every violated split has entries in {0,±1}.
- Gap-0 separation is NP-complete (from PARTITION; strong hardness not shown), but only at non-psd points, where psd separation already finds a cut.
- Still open: general gap inequalities at psd points. My construction does not control them there.

Exact rational checks, a single-threaded SCIP cross-check and numerical probes all agree with the theorems. An unsuccessful search does not establish novelty; the full Deza–Laurent chapter was not accessible.

results.claim: Literature status: every source checked (Avis-Grishukhin 1993 §4; DGL 1993 Remark 4.12 p.51; Deza-Laurent 1997 Ch.28 abstract; Avis 2003 §1; Letchford-Sorensen 2012 pp.269-270; GKL 2012 §4 p.151) states hypermetric/rounded psd/gap-1/odd clique/gap-0 separation complexity as unknown; web, arXiv and Crossref searches found no later source settling it. The split note's 'open' statement was an accurate literature report but is now superseded.

Theorem 1: for an exact-cover instance S_1..S_n ⊆ [p] (p≥2) and max(p/8,(p-2)/4) ≤ η² < p/4, the PD matrix M_ij=4δ_ij+|S_i∩S_j|, M_ig=|S_i|/2, M_gg=p/4+η² has g_M(z)=z^TMz-Σ M_ii z_i <0 exactly at z=(x,-1) with x an exact cover, value -(p/2-2η²).
results.location: note.md §3 (Lemma 1, Theorem 1, Corollary 1: d_0i=4+|S_i|, d_0g=(2p-1)/4, d_ij=8+|S_iΔS_j|, d_ig=(2p+15)/4)

results.claim: Corollary 2: HYP-VIOLATION (does rational d violate some hypermetric inequality?) is strongly NP-complete; hypermetric cone membership is strongly co-NP-complete (answers Avis-Grishukhin P1). NP membership by an elementary lemma (Lemma 2).
Lemma 3: polynomial cases: non-negative-type points, non-spherical psd points, fixed gonality, fixed support; FPT (r^{O(r)} poly) in rank of M.

Corollary 3: for X3C with q≥K≥3 the hard d is of negative type with PD Gram matrix, satisfies all triangle and all hypermetric inequalities of gonality ≤2K-3; the binary point X(ε), ε=1/(2δ^TM^{-1}δ), is PD with X_ii=X_0i, lies in the metric polytope and elliptope; its violated splits are exactly (0,-x,1),(-1,x,-1) with value -ε/2; no rounded psd inequality with |σ|≥3 is violated. Triangle inequalities hold iff no exact cover uses ≤2 sets.

Corollary 4: separation of hypermetric (= hypermetric correlation), gap-1, rounded psd (= Boros-Hammer = binary split), and k-gonal over all k is strongly NP-complete, even at the points of Corollary 3.
Corollary 5: with q-2 copies of point 0, pure hypermetric and odd clique separation are strongly NP-complete (hard points are semimetrics with repeated points).
Corollary 6: the split note's SPLIT-SEP stays strongly NP-complete at PD points with X_ii=X_0i satisfying all Boolean quadric triangle inequalities; violated splits have entries in {0,±1}.

Theorem 4: gap-0 separation is NP-complete (reduction from PARTITION via an explicit unit-diagonal Z with one tiny negative eigenvalue along a). Gap-0 inequalities never cut psd points. Strong NP-hardness not shown.

Exact-arithmetic verification: closed form (300 cases), Theorem 1 on 840 exact-cover/X3C instances, cut form, binary point (all violated splits enumerated completely by Fincke-Pohst over every odd u_0), gonality, pure violators, controls (η²=p/4 kills violators; η²=p/16 creates k≤-2 violators); gap-0 construction on 40 instances (all s checked exactly). 0 failures.
Independent SCIP 10.0 (PySCIPOpt 6.2.1) cross-check on 24 X3C instances: minimum of z^T(4M)z - diag(4M)^Tz over a box containing all violators is -2 iff a cover exists, else 0.

At scaled hard points of no-instances (48 instances, 4-8 points, small coefficient boxes) no violated general gap inequality was found; in 24 no-instances with 7-10 points εd lies in the cut polytope (LP).
The hard points cannot lie in the cut polytope for all no-instances unless NP = co-NP (Carathéodory certificate argument), so the cut-cone observation does not settle general gap separation.

corrections_to_earlier_notes: Split note (research-20260928b/side-results/split-separation-np-complete.md), Summary 'Novelty caveat', §6 'The binary analogue is open' and §8 last Limits bullet: accurate as a literature report, but now superseded. Hypermetric, gap-1 and rounded psd (Boros-Hammer/binary split) separation are strongly NP-complete, also at PD binary points inside the psd and triangle relaxations (note.md Corollaries 3, 4, 6).

Split note §6 'These are the rounded psd inequalities of Galli-Kaparis-Letchford': imprecise attribution. GKL 2012 §2 cite five earlier sources; the name 'rounded psd' is used in Letchford-Sorensen 2012 (10); in Boolean quadric form these are the Boros-Hammer inequalities (Boros-Hammer 1993; GKL 2011 (6); LS 2012 (8)).
Split note §6 'GKL also note that rounded psd separation reduces to hypermetric separation': correct, but the reduction is Letchford-Sorensen 2012 Prop. 19 (GKL's Theorem 3).

Split note §6 cites only the GKL 2011 preprint; the published ORL 40 (2012), §4, p. 151 has the same sentence. Bibliographic note: GKL 2012 cite Laurent-Poljak 'Gap inequalities for the cut polytope' as SIAM J. Matrix Anal. 17 (1996) 530-547. Per Crossref it is Eur. J. Combin. 17 (1996) 233-254; the SIAM pages belong to 'On the facial structure of the set of correlation matrices'.

Split note §6 'does not settle the binary case': true for that construction, but the Delaunay obstruction is not intrinsic; exact cover meets it. The 'post-2012 hypermetric literature was not searched' gap is now filled: no resolution found.
research-20260928b/reviews/split-separation-review.md §8.3 ('still open'): superseded in the same way. The quotations checked in split-final-review.md remain correct as quotations.
open_questions: Is separation of general gap inequalities NP-hard at psd points? Is it in NP? GKL give only a doubly exponential algorithm.
Is odd clique separation NP-hard at points with positive definite Gram matrix (no repeated points)?
Is approximating the normalized maximum hypermetric/rounded psd violation hard, e.g. within a constant additive gap at elliptope points? The violation at the hard psd points here is Θ(1/(n+p)).
Can the hard points be made to satisfy all gap inequalities with γ≥3? They cannot all lie in the cut polytope unless NP = co-NP.
Novelty: the construction may be folklore. The full Deza–Laurent Ch. 28 (§28.3, p. 454), Laurent–Poljak 1996, Boros–Hammer 1993, Erdahl 1992 and Dash's thesis were not read.
solver_relevance: Modest. Unless P = NP, exact polynomial-time separation of hypermetric, gap-1, rounded psd, Boros–Hammer and odd clique inequalities is impossible, even at points that already satisfy the SDP relaxation, all triangle inequalities and the fixed-gonality families. That supports what BiqMac, BiqBin and MADAM already do (enumerate triangle, pentagonal and heptagonal inequalities) and GKL's heuristics: bounding gonality or support makes separation polynomial. It gives no guidance on which heuristic works. The violations at the hard points are only polynomially small, and the gap-0 result has no practical effect. Nothing was measured on solvers, and I did not check whether SCIP 10.0 separates any of these classes.
